chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Sahban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Mis'mam Abi Sayyar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Three tasbihs (glorifications) or their equivalent, recited with a flowing/deliberate pace, suffice for you in the speech of bowing and prostration; and it is not incumbent upon you, nor is it a matter of honor, to say 'Subhan, Subhan, Subhan' (Glory, Glory, Glory)."

key_terms.كَرَامَةَ: Honor/Excellence (in this context, a specific reward or status)
key_terms.مُتَرَسِّلًا: With a flowing, deliberate, or measured pace

ai.seo_question: What is the sufficient dhikr for ruku and sujood in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling to clarify the flexibility in the dhikr of ruku' and sujood, emphasizing that the spiritual quality of 'mutarrassilan' (deliberate and flowing) outweighs rigid verbal formulae. This reflects the Shia scholarly preference for meaningful, measured remembrance over mechanical repetition, ensuring the worshipper maintains presence of heart (khushu') during the physical acts of prayer.
